# Test fixtures

## clip-60fps-60frames.mp4

A one second synthetic clip: 320x240, **constant 60 frames per second,
exactly 60 frames**, H.264 in MP4. No faces, no people, just a test
pattern.

It exists because the end to end tests used to build their clip inside
the browser with `MediaRecorder`. That works on a developer's Mac and
does not work in WebKit on Linux, where `MediaRecorder` does not exist
at all, so the cross-browser tests could never run in continuous
integration.

A committed binary is normally worth avoiding, because nobody can
review one. Two things make this one acceptable: it is generated by a
single reproducible command, recorded below, and it contains nothing
but a synthetic pattern. Regenerate it and the bytes should match.

60 frames at 60 per second is the point. A slower clip cannot catch a
stepper that lets frames slip, which is exactly the bug that shipped
twice on this project.

```
ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i "testsrc2=size=320x240:rate=60:duration=1" \
  -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -g 12 -an \
  test/fixtures/clip-60fps-60frames.mp4
```

Verify the frame count with:

```
ffmpeg -v quiet -stats -i test/fixtures/clip-60fps-60frames.mp4 \
  -map 0:v -f null -
```

## Whose face this is

`session-01.json` is **the author's own face**, recorded with the dev-only
"Record fixture" button and confirmed by the owner on 2026-08-15. The same is
true of `analysis/tests/fixtures/session-fixture.csv`, which carries real
`kss_before` and `kss_after` sleepiness ratings.

This is written down because an audit found it stated nowhere. Face geometry
and a self-reported sleepiness score are personal data, and a reader of a
public repository could not otherwise tell consent from oversight.
